source.title: Latent Instruction Representation Alignment: defending against jailbreaks, backdoors and undesired knowledge in LLMs

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates unlearning outcomes using its own method and compares them with gradient difference and RMU, but does not test the recovery attacks in the claim.
record.gate_note: The WMDP Cyber and TOFU results measure forgetting and retention, not recovery after unlearning. The paper does not fine-tune unlearned models on recovery data, ablate an activation direction, quantize weights, or test prompt-only recovery. The representation plot is an analysis of forget/retain representation distributions, not a test that the knowledge remains recoverable.
record.test_reason: The study measures how far LIRA, RMU and gradient difference lower forget-set multiple-choice accuracy and raise free-response cross-entropy on WMDP Cyber and TOFU, while tracking retain-set CE and MMLU. That bears on the first half of version A: near-chance target accuracy with general ability kept. It runs no recovery attack on any unlearned model (no relearning, ablation, quantization or prompting), so the attack-resistance half of A and versions B–F are untested. Its PEZ and embedding-space attacks target harmful-request compliance, not unlearned knowledge.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors also claim 'optimal forgetting' on WMDP Cyber with negligible benign loss, and say weak baseline performance agrees with Lynch et al. (2024). They concede LIRA does not stop an attacker who fine-tunes, and the knowledge may be inexpressible rather than removed.
record.recipe_differences: The study introduces LIRA and classifier-guided LIRA; it does not reproduce the cited unlearning-recovery attack recipes or test post-unlearning recovery.
record.method_sensitivity: WMDP's forget/retain boundary is described as a coherent abstract property, whereas TOFU's forget-retain boundary is arbitrary; the authors characterize TOFU as a difficult case for LIRA.

fits_no_version.finding: After LIRA, WMDP forget and retain prompt representations at layer 27 are almost indistinguishable along the initial discriminant. After RMU they stay separated.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Classifier-guided LIRA removes the linear separability of forget- and retain-domain prompt representations. This alone does not show whether the knowledge is deleted or recoverable.

fits_no_version.finding: Gradient difference raises forget free-response CE strongly while MC accuracy on the same knowledge barely changes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Output-level unlearning (GD) can suppress verbalization while MC probing still shows the knowledge, a form of shallow unlearning seen through evaluation format rather than an attack.

record.problems: The study does not test the specified recovery attacks. Its WMDP data are synthetic question-answer pairs generated and filtered with Gemini 2.0 Flash, and the authors acknowledge that WMDP includes some questions they judge benign. TOFU evaluation questions were pruned because some could be answered without the taught information. Reported table values are extracted from flattened table text; plots report 90% confidence intervals and results aggregate at least three runs.
record.rows_left_out: The tables also report retain-set cross-entropy and MMLU changes for multiple methods. Their model-to-value alignment is ambiguous in the supplied flattened table text, so those values were not assigned to individual rows. The paper's qualitative statements that LIRA has minimal impact on retained and general capabilities are reflected in the verdict and authors' conclusion.

untested.parts: Whether simple attacks (relearning, prompting, quantization, ablation) recover knowledge from LIRA- or RMU-unlearned models.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or relearning test.
No direction ablation or analysis of whether knowledge is stored but blocked. Fig. 3a only shows forget and retain prompt representations overlapping.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, language or in-context recovery on unlearned models. Jailbreak tests target harmful-request compliance only.
LIRA is presented as robust, but no recovery attack is run against its unlearning. The authors state it does not stop an attacker who can fine-tune.

missing.what: Retain-set CE and MMLU changes per method and model. Readable values: Gemma WMDP retain CE LIRA +0.0, GD +1.9, RMU +0.0 and MMLU +0.1%/+0.9%/+0.1%. LLaMA WMDP retain CE +0.0/+1.1/+0.0, MMLU apparently +3.1%/-1.8%/+0.0%. Gemma TOFU retain CE +0.0/+4.6/+0.0. These are needed for the 'keeps general ability' part of A.
Baseline WMDP accuracy for Gemma 2 9B (58%) and the derived floor of about 0.30 against LIRA's 37%. Neither is stored as a row baseline.

record.verdict_notes: This is a methods paper (LIRA) that covers jailbreaks, backdoors and unlearning. Its unlearning evidence is forget/retain measurement only, so it bears on the pre-attack half of A. The jailbreak results (PEZ, embedding-space) concern refusal of harmful requests, not recovery of unlearned knowledge, and should not be linked to E or F. Classifier-guided LIRA stops on a threshold set directly on forget-set MC accuracy (Table 13: while accuracy ≥38% on WMDP, ≥18% on TOFU), so its final accuracy partly reflects the stopping rule. The WMDP training data are Gemini-generated Q&A, and the TOFU evaluation was pruned, so neither matches the original benchmarks.

versions.untested_parts: The study evaluates whether unlearning reduces target-set performance while retaining other capabilities, but does not test whether simple attacks recover the knowledge.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or relearning-set recovery test.
No activation-direction ablation or test establishing that targeted knowledge remains stored but inaccessible.
No prompt-rephrasing, jailbreak, language, or in-context recovery test after unlearning.
LIRA is presented as a robustness and unlearning method, but the study does not test whether it resists the recovery attacks specified in the claim.

source_check.notes: Tables 6/7 are flattened. Forget acc, forget CE and retain CE place by line order (Gemma, then LLaMA, then TOFU Gemma), but the MMLU cells for LLaMA are ambiguous (orphan +3.1%/-1.8%/+0.0%). RMU on Gemma WMDP lands near 34% (58-24.0), close to LIRA's 37%, so R9 observed vs R1 partial (and l0 vs l1) rests on a 3-point gap. GD forget CE rose sharply (+35.5, +5.2, +29.8) even though MC barely moved. No recovery attack is tested, and the authors concede LIRA may make knowledge inexpressible rather than remove it.
